about.title: Milpitas Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Milpitas sits at the meeting point of I-880, I-680 and Route 237, and a lot of what moves through the city moves in boxes — components, consumer electronics, tools, and vehicles headed to homes and workplaces across Santa Clara County. When one of those products fails and someone gets hurt, California law takes a practical view. You usually do not have to prove the manufacturer was careless. If the design was flawed, a unit came off the line wrong, or the warnings left out a real risk, and that defect caused your injury, strict liability can apply. Responsibility may reach the maker, the distributor, and the store that sold it. The single most useful thing you can do is keep the product exactly as it is — do not repair it, return it, or throw it away. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm. We connect Milpitas residents with an independent product liability attorney who works on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Milpitas Residents Use LawProactive for Product Claims

items.title: You Usually Don't Have to Prove Negligence
items.desc: California product liability often runs on strict liability: showing a design, manufacturing or warning defect caused your injury is generally enough. The attorney we connect you with knows how to frame the claim that way.

items.title: Every Link in the Chain Can Be Examined
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors and retailers may all share responsibility for a defective product. An independent attorney can sort out who belongs in the claim rather than letting one company point at another.

items.title: Preserving the Evidence Comes First
items.desc: The product itself is the heart of the case, and an attorney can arrange to have it stored and inspected properly. Our connection is free, and network attorneys work on contingency.

items.question: My airbag didn't deploy in a crash on I-880 near Milpitas. Is that a car accident claim or a product claim?
items.answer: It can be both. The other driver may be responsible for the collision, while the vehicle or airbag manufacturer may be responsible under strict liability if a defect made your injuries worse. Keep the car exactly as it is and do not authorize repairs or salvage until an attorney has looked at it. Public records show I-880, I-680 and Route 237 carry the largest share of collisions in the city, so this question comes up more than you might expect.

items.question: Do I need proof that the company knew the product was faulty?
items.answer: Generally, no. Under California's strict liability approach, the focus is on whether the product had a design, manufacturing or warning defect and whether that defect caused your injury. What the company knew or intended is usually not something you have to establish. An attorney can explain how this applies to your specific product.

items.question: I already threw away the box and receipt. Does that end my claim?
items.answer: Not necessarily, though it does make the product itself even more important to keep. Purchase history from a bank statement, online order, or store loyalty account can often stand in for a paper receipt. Photos of the product, the injury, and the scene help too. Bring whatever you have and let the attorney assess it.
